title: Partial-stream reconciliation and schema fidelity checksuite
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Build a regression-grade checksuite that validates JSON-mode enforcement, constrained decoding backoffs, and schema adherence across partial streaming responses and interleaved tool/function calls. The harness should emulate realistic production characteristics (prefix cache hits, mid-stream truncation, network jitter, and multi-model fallbacks) and provide deterministic failure modes for SLO/regression tracking. Goals:
- Exercise decoder behavior when token emissions are interrupted and later resumed (partial-emit + rejoin).
- Validate tool-call sentinel placement and how that affects downstream JSON-structure assembly.
- Confirm graceful degradation paths (constrained-decoder backoff -> relaxed-schema reparse -> fallback model) preserve structural validity or surface clear repair guidance.
- Produce telemetry and canonical failure signatures to feed into the console's regression alerts and rollouts dashboard.
Links to artifacts: PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-structured-output-recon; design spec: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/structured-output/recon-spec.pdf; prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recon-checksuite/tree/eng-981761
acceptance_criteria:
1) Checksuite runs against a matrix of 6 model variants and produces a deterministic classification for each test (pass / schema-violation / partial-emission-recovery / toolcall-mismatch).
2) Simulated partial-stream scenarios (cut at random token boundaries, at toolcall boundaries, and mid-json-field) are covered with reproducible seeds.
3) For any schema violations, the harness must output: failing example input, model seed, token-offset where violation began, and recommended fallback route (e.g., decoder-backoff, model-variant, or schema-relax).
4) Integration: one can kick off the checksuite via CI job that uploads summarized telemetry to the Console canary dashboard and creates a Regression issue when severity is high.
5) Automated canary using 5% prod-like traffic mirror that runs the lightweight subset without affecting latency SLOs.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for the token-wrangler and reassembly logic.
- Synthetic fuzz driver that injects jitter, drop, and re-order events.
- End-to-end runs against dedicated staging cluster (dedicated GPU pool) with KV cache enabled and disabled.
- Cross-compat runs with streaming SDK and HTTP chunked streaming to catch client decoder edge cases.
- Run the full matrix nightly and store results in the checksuite artifact bucket for diffing.
- Record baseline run and schedule weekly regression comparisons.
updates: 2025-08-12: kickoff meeting — alignment with PM (Lina Chen) and Design (Marco Rami). Decided to prioritize streaming+toolcall interplay over cheaper static parse tests.
2025-08-18: prototype harness (token reassembly + seedable partial-cut simulator) finished. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recon-checksuite/pull/17

2025-08-21: discovered case where toolcall sentinel emitted inside an object field causes two competing parses. Recorded example and added a targeted test that reproduces sentinel-in-middle-of-object behavior.

2025-08-26: design review — trade-off: strict immediate-fail on first schema violation vs. attempt greedy repair. Chosen approach: mark violation and attempt safe repair path only in non-customer-impacting baseline runs; canary will remain strict.

2025-08-30: telemetry schema for failure signatures drafted (fields: test_id, model_variant, seed, token_offset, violation_type, suggested_fallback). Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/TV-telemetry
2025-09-01: integrated lightweight canary job into CI; initial nightly matrix runs green for 4/6 model variants. Two variants show repeatable 'truncated-array' failures under high-jitter config.
2025-09-02: opened fix spike ENG-981762 to add decoder-backoff policy and toolcall-rewrite step; added dependency on ENG-960010 (streaming-sdk-chunk-reassembly-fix).
